title: Pack the order that fits and flag the one that cannot, instead of forcing it
instruction: Pack the blue blocks into the blue box and the orange blocks into the orange box, each block lying flat inside its box and below the rim. If an order cannot all fit in its box, pack none of that order and put the red card on the flag pad of the same colour as that order instead.
context: Hand packers pack the orders that fit and flag an order for a larger carton when it does not, rather than overfilling it (crush damage, a lid that will not close) or shipping it short. The robot has to judge each order: packing everything and flagging everything both fail. The judgement is about the whole set against the box's capacity, not whether each item fits on its own: every orange block fits the orange box alone.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. All blocks are pale wood (600 kg/m3), 30 mm thick, lying flat on a 30 mm side, square to the table edges; sizes are given front to back by across. Blue order (in front of the left arm): the blue box (fixed, blue-painted card walls 5 mm thick and 34 mm tall around an inside of 170 mm front to back by 115 mm across, open top, the table as its floor), centred 33.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 20.0 cm left of the midline; blue block A, 90 x 60 mm, 97 g, centred 17.0 cm in front and 24.0 cm left; blue block B, 60 x 60 mm, 65 g, at 17.0 cm and 35.5 cm left; blue block C, 140 x 35 mm, 88 g, at 17.5 cm and 11.5 cm left. Orange order (in front of the right arm): the orange box (fixed, orange-painted card walls 5 mm thick and 34 mm tall around an inside of 150 mm front to back by 100 mm across), centred 33.0 cm in front and 20.0 cm right of the midline; orange blocks A and B, 60 x 80 mm, 86 g each, centred 16.0 cm in front at 10.0 cm and 20.5 cm right; orange block C, 50 x 70 mm, 63 g, at 16.0 cm and 30.0 cm right; orange block D, 60 x 60 mm, 65 g, at 24.5 cm in front and 35.5 cm right. Two fixed flag pads (plastic sheets 80 x 80 mm, 2 mm thick), both centred 34.0 cm in front: the blue pad 5.5 cm left of the midline and the orange pad 5.5 cm right. Red card (loose, solid red plastic block standing in for a flag card, 60 mm front to back, 40 mm across, 25 mm tall, 70 g), lying flat at 23.0 cm in front on the midline. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored at the end of the trial, in two halves. Terms: a block lies flat when its 30 mm axis is within 5 degrees of vertical; it rests on the table (or a box floor, which is the table) when its lowest point is at most 1 mm above the table and it is at rest (moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s); it is in a box when its centre is over the box's outer footprint, walls included, seen from above; it is packed when it is in its own box, lies flat, rests on the floor and its highest point is at most 34 mm above the table (not above the rim). The card is on a pad when its centre is over the pad, its lowest point is at most 1 mm above the pad's top (any face down, not held above it) and it is at rest. Blue half (up to 0.5): 0 if the card is on the blue pad (a packable order flagged); otherwise 0.5 x (blue blocks packed) / 3, so a blue block sticking up above the rim or propped on another earns nothing but does not cancel the others. Orange half (up to 0.5): 0 unless the card is on the orange pad; then 0.5 if every orange block lies flat resting on the table outside both boxes (anywhere, any way round; a flag pad counts as table: lowest point at most 1 mm above the pad's top), 0.25 if every orange block is either that or packed in the orange box (flagged but not emptied), and 0 otherwise (an orange block above the rim, stacked, leaning on a box or anything else, not flat, in the blue box, off the table or moving). Score = blue half + orange half, so packing everything or flagging everything earns at most 0.5. Trying to pack and then taking blocks out again is allowed. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step.
reset_notes: Lay every block and the card back at its starting place, flat and square; empty both boxes. In the real rig the boxes and pads are taped to the table. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Every object is a rigid box; each carton is four fixed walls with the table as its floor and cannot bulge or be crushed. The blocks stand in for the orders' items and the red block for a flag card. Friction is the simulator's default.
